understanding the contact resistance between TiSi2and diffusions and its impact on CMOS circuit performance.
the impact of silicide to diffusion contacts on circuit performance and the process conditions that are necessary to minimize this contact resistance.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of silicides to enhance CMOS performance is not as straight forward as one might expect.
the silicide to n-type diffusion contact resistance is the most important process variable in the silicide process flow.
the use of silicides in submicron CMOS technology can have a significant impact on the performance and yield of the circuit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of silicide-clad diffusions in 1-μm CMOS technology requires that the silicide to n-type diffusion contact resistance be kept below a value of 5 × 10-8Ωcm2.
, for the first time, the contact resistivity between silicide and diffusion has been quantified and the effect of this parameter on the performance of 1-µ CMOS circuitry has been evaluated.
the use of silicides to enhance diffusion resistance can be detrimental to the performance of the underlying transistors unless care is taken to minimize the silicideto diffusion contact resistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the contact resistivity between the silicide and the diffusion is an important parameter in the optimization of 1-µ CMOS technology.
the use of silicides to reduce the sheet resistance of diffusions does not guarantee a corresponding reduction in contact resistance.
the contact resistivity of silicide to diffusion junctions is a critical parameter in 1-µM CMOS circuit design and that it must be carefully controlled to ensure the desired circuit performance.
